leads.title: Criminal Law (Offences) Act (1893) - Sections 351 and 353
leads.documents: Criminalization of same-sex sexual activity in Guyana: Sec.351 gross indecency between males (2 years imprisonment), Sec.353 buggery (felony, life imprisonment); colonial British origin retained after independence.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as 'Criminal Law (Offences) Act (1893)' with quoted text of Section 351 and Section 353

leads.title: Caribbean Court of Justice - Quincy McEwan, Seon Clarke, Joseph Fraser, Seyon Persaud and SASOD v The Attorney General of Guyana
leads.documents: 13 November 2018 final ruling striking down Section 153(1)(XLVII) Summary Jurisdiction (Offences) Act criminalizing cross-dressing as unconstitutional, archaic, vague, violating protection of law and rule of law; oral arguments began 28 June 2018.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail: CCJ, 5-judge panel, decided 13 November 2018, case name as listed

leads.title: Summary Jurisdiction (Offences) Act - Section 153(1)(XLVII)
leads.documents: Former cross-dressing prohibition used to arrest transgender activists in 2009; litigated 2010-2018 as discriminatory and unconstitutional due to vagueness of 'improper purpose' and savings clause issue.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as Section 153(1)(XLVII) at issue in Guyana Trans United challenge

leads.title: Guyana Supreme Court (Chief Justice Ian Chang, 2013) and Guyana Court of Appeal - cross-dressing case
leads.documents: Intermediate rulings that cross-dressing was legal unless done for an 'improper purpose'; Court of Appeal upheld Chang before appeal to CCJ; shows enforcement history and rights machinery.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail: 2010 challenge by Guyana Trans United, 2013 ruling by Chief Justice Ian Chang, subsequent Court of Appeal affirmance

leads.title: Constitution of Guyana - savings clause; National Assembly constitutional amendment efforts
leads.documents: Savings clause preventing judicial review of British colonial-era laws even if violating human rights - impediment to decriminalization; December 2000 unanimous amendment to prohibit sexual orientation discrimination denied assent by President Bharrat Jagdeo; 2003 clause withdrawn.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited in decriminalization and discrimination protections sections, with 2000-2001 and 2003 parliamentary history

leads.title: U.S. Department of State - Guyana adoption guidance; Guyana Childcare and Protection Act
leads.documents: LGBTQ person not disqualified from adopting; both married and single people may adopt; CPA Director December 2015 statement that CPA does not discriminate and encourages LGBTQ adoptive/foster parents/guardians.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail: 'According to the U.S. Department of State' and 'Director of Guyana's Childcare and Protection Agency (CPA)' December 2015 statement under Childcare and Protection Act

leads.title: Guyana Government CEDAW Ninth Periodic Report - Geneva presentation July 2019 by Minister of Social Protection Amna Ally
leads.documents: Official government statement that Guyana is working to remove all legal gaps to prevent discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity; that everyone has inherent right to live free from violence, abuse and discrimination.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail: presentation of Guyana's statement on ninth periodic report on implementation of CEDAW in Geneva, Switzerland, July 2019

leads.title: Society Against Sexual Orientation Discrimination (SASOD) - Law Reform Commission advocacy and police extortion / hate-crime reporting; Ministry of Social Protection condemnation
leads.documents: May 2019 hope Law Reform Commission will update archaic laws; managing director Joel Simpson May 2019 statement that discriminatory laws contribute to extortion by law enforcement and under-reported hate crimes; June 16 2019 alleged homophobic attack on Simpson at Bourda Market and call for hate-crime legislation.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail: SASOD May 2019, June 2019 Bourda Market/Palm Court incident, police complaint 16 June, assailant surrender 8 July 2019

leads.title: Guyana Court of Appeal - Clive Knights case (July 2019) - gay panic defence
leads.documents: Reduction of 2012 murder conviction of Bert Whyte from murder (57 years, June 2015 jury verdict) to manslaughter (30 years) after claim of 'unwanted homosexual advances' and fatal stabbing; documents court treatment of anti-gay violence.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; citation detail: Guyana Court of Appeal July 2019, victim Bert Whyte (2012), defendant Clive Knights

leads.title: Caribbean Development Research Services Inc. (CADRES) 2013 survey and SASOD-commissioned October 2022 poll 'perceptions and attitudes towards LGBT Persons in Guyana'; LAPOP Vanderbilt AmericasBarometer 2010 and 2017
leads.documents: Population-level enforcement risk context: 2013 24% hate, 38% tolerant, 25% accepting, 53% supported criminalization; 2022 12% hatred, 72.4% accept/tolerate (n=1,070); same-sex marriage support 14% (2013 CADRES), 7.2/100 (2010 LAPOP) rising to 20.6 (2017).
